summary: Vibe Calibration autonomously calibrates a 112-qubit frequency-tunable transmon processor by orchestrating reusable Skills through a fine-tuned LLM agent, achieving 108/112 qubits in 4.7 hours with 4–5× speedup over manual operation. The system distills expert tacit knowledge via three-phase human-in-the-loop training and demonstrates transfer of calibration workflows across devices without retraining.
motivation: Manual calibration of superconducting processors becomes intractable at scale; conventional scripts are brittle to anomalies, and expert judgment is bounded by cognitive bandwidth and serial operation time, creating a bottleneck that prevents scaling toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Expert experimental trajectories are distilled into two complementary training datasets ($\mathcal{D}_A$ for step-level behavior cloning with full tool schemas preserved, $\mathcal{D}_B$ for domain knowledge with 6–8 paraphrased surface forms per semantic atom). Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is fine-tuned via LoRA-Over on both datasets; the resulting checkpoint operates as a Claude-Code agent that follows a qubit-characterization Skill organized as a decision tree with explicit quality gates ($R^2 > 0.9$, SNR $\geq 10$ dB), rollback edges, and audit records.
result: On 112 transmons with $E_C/h \approx 190$ MHz, $E_J^{\mathrm{max}}/h \approx 12.97–13.56$ GHz, the agent achieves $T_1 = 96.2$ µs (median, 108/112 qubits), $T_2^R = 7.9$ µs (median, 102/112 qubits), and completes in 4.7 h; expert comparison on 16-qubit subset shows agreement on 14/16 qubits (87.5%) with paired $t$-test $p = 0.31$ for $T_1$ and $p = 0.42$ for $T_2^R$; cross-chip transfer test on unseen 16-qubit architecture shows the 35B-$\mathcal{D}_A$ checkpoint successfully loads and follows new Skills in all 6 sessions without memorizing training patterns.
